messages.content: You are a meticulous energy-infrastructure research agent. Your task in Phase B is to produce a primary-sourced inventory of Vietnam thermal generation assets >30 MWe, following the user’s schema exactly. Use retrieval tools aggressively but budget-consciously; do not use tools that delegate reasoning to another model. Distinguish discovery sources from justification sources: tertiary sources may generate leads only, never final support. Final claims must be supported by admissible sources: official government documents, regulator/utility official data, operator filings/press releases, international-institution reports, bylined trade press, or industry trackers exposing primary provenance. Prefer Vietnamese official sources, EVN/PV Power/PV GAS/Petrovietnam/Vinacomin/TKV/GENCO/PECC/BOT sponsor sources, PDP7/PDP8 implementation documents, annual reports, environmental approvals, project pages, and official dispatches. Never fabricate URLs, source titles, or citations. If a known asset cannot be sourced, include it with Source = "not found", LOW confidence, and a Notes explanation. Maintain calibrated confidence: HIGH requires at least two independent concordant sources with at least one primary; MEDIUM requires one primary or sourced aggregator with verifiable primary; LOW for secondary-only, inferred, stale, conflicted, or unsourced claims; apply hard ceilings for self-reports and stale status. Use exact status terms: Announced, Pre-permit, Permitted, Construction, Operating, Shelved, Cancelled, Retired. Use exact fuel terms: Coal, Domestic gas, Imported LNG. Use exact technology terms: Subcritical, Supercritical, USC, CCGT, OCGT. Treat coal and gas plants at the same power center as separate rows when ownership, financing, COD, status, or unit group differs. Include all past, present, future, shelved, cancelled, and retired thermal assets in Vietnam above 30 MWe, excluding oil/diesel/biomass unless needed only as an explanatory note because the required final Fuel vocabulary is limited to Coal, Domestic gas, and Imported LNG. If a gas project’s source is ambiguous between domestic gas and LNG, choose the best-supported value, mark confidence appropriately, and explain. Be temporally explicit: every row needs Status as-of-date, using a source publication/effective date or a clearly stated best-effort date. Before finalizing, run a verification pass for duplicate rows, arithmetic consistency, status vocabulary, source admissibility, date freshness, and whether citations actually support claims. Output in Phase B must be a single Markdown document that begins directly with exactly one pipe table and has no title or preamble. After the table, include concise per-asset/project explanatory notes only where warranted, then an annotated bibliography of every source cited. Do not add any additional pipe tables, summary tables, or markdown table-like structures.

Produce the requested Vietnam thermal generation asset inventory (>30 MWe) in the fixed Phase B format. Work in stages under the budget: first build and verify the candidate asset list using broad discovery, then replace discovery leads with admissible sources, then produce the final Markdown document. You may use up to three planning/search turns before the report; do not rush the final report on turn 1 if source coverage is incomplete. Retrieval priorities: (1) Vietnam PDP8 and PDP8 implementation-plan decisions and appendices; (2) EVN, GENCO, PV Power, PV GAS/Petrovietnam, TKV/Vinacomin, provincial or ministry documents; (3) project company/BOT sponsor filings and press releases; (4) EIA/approval/financing documents from MONRE, MOIT, World Bank, ADB, JICA/JBIC, IFC, OECD/Equator-bank documents; (5) bylined trade press and industry trackers only where they expose or corroborate primary sources. Use tertiary sources only for leads, never as Source 1 or Source 2. Include coal, domestic-gas, and imported-LNG thermal power assets above 30 MWe at all lifecycle stages, including operating, retired, construction, planned, shelved, and cancelled. Follow the row-granularity rule: default to plant/unit-group rows; split co-located phases/projects when capacity, COD, owner, fuel, status, or financing differs; aggregate only if evidence is unavailable and label ambiguity. The final response must be one Markdown document beginning immediately with exactly one pipe table with columns, in order: Name (Vietnamese), Name (English), Province, Fuel (Coal / Domestic gas / Imported LNG), Technology (Subcritical / Supercritical / USC for coal; CCGT / OCGT for gas), Units × MW, Total MWe, Status, Status as-of-date, COD, Owner/Developer, Confidence, Source 1, Source 2, Notes. After the single table, add concise sourced notes for major/disputed/ambiguous/historically important assets only, then an annotated bibliography listing every cited source with full citation, URL when available, original-language title plus English translation for Vietnamese/non-English sources, and a short annotation. No overview, no title, no statistical summary table, and no second pipe table. If uncertain, mark LOW and explain; if exact source handle cannot be located, write "URL not verified" rather than inventing it.

**Notes on scope, uncertainty, and row granularity.** This inventory applies the requested >30 MWe threshold to coal, domestic-gas, and imported-LNG thermal assets only. Oil/diesel-only plants and biomass/waste-heat projects were excluded even where above 30 MWe because the required fuel vocabulary is limited. Where Vietnamese planning documents use power-center or project-stage names rather than built plant names, rows retain the Vietnamese planning name and are marked LOW or MEDIUM rather than forcing false unit detail. Decision 262/QĐ-TTg dated 1 April 2024 is the main current planning source for PDP8 implementation; Decision 1509/QĐ-BCT dated 30 May 2025 is the main retrieved source for the adjusted PDP8 implementation framework, but the accessible English text did not include full appendices, so rows relying only on those appendices are confidence-capped. ([datafiles.chinhphu.vn](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2024/4/262-ttg.signed.pdf))

**Coal technology caveat.** Several Vietnamese coal plants use circulating fluidized-bed boilers, especially Vinacomin/TKV’s Na Duong, Cao Ngan, Son Dong, Cam Pha, Mao Khe, and Nong Son group. Because the schema permits only Subcritical, Supercritical, or USC for coal, CFB units are classified as Subcritical unless a supercritical/USC source was verified. Vinacomin’s own cited article describes these as CFB coal plants with named capacities, but not as supercritical units. ([vietnamenergy.vn](https://vietnamenergy.vn/vinacomin-has-successfully-applied-cfb-technology-in-the-thermal-power-plants-18781.html?utm_source=openai))

**Gas fuel caveat.** O Mon 1 is historically associated with fuel oil and delayed domestic gas supply, but PDP8 implementation materials explicitly treat existing/Block B-related O Mon gas-to-power projects within the domestic-gas plan. It is therefore classified as Domestic gas, with notes. Decision 1509 also directs the national energy group to accelerate domestic gas fields including Block B, Ca Voi Xanh, and Ken Bau for power generation. ([datafiles.chinhphu.vn](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2024/4/262-ttg.signed.pdf?utm_source=openai))

**LNG status caveat.** Most LNG projects are planning-stage assets rather than operating plants. Decision 262 was retrieved with a direct government PDF handle and its excerpt indicates tables for domestic gas and LNG projects; Mayer Brown’s bylined legal update corroborates that Decision 262 gave status updates for 13 imported LNG power projects and 10 domestic gas-fired projects totaling 22,400 MW and 14,930 MW respectively. Rows remain MEDIUM or LOW unless direct project-company, investment-approval, or construction proof was also retrieved. ([datafiles.chinhphu.vn](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2024/4/262-ttg.signed.pdf?utm_source=openai))

**Concise notes for major, disputed, ambiguous, or historically important assets**

PDP8 and adjusted-PDP8 planning sources are authoritative for the inclusion of planned gas/LNG/coal projects, but the accessible text of Decision 1509 states that the detailed project lists are in appendices not translated in the retrieved page. Therefore, projects depending only on Decision 1509’s inaccessible appendices are marked LOW unless also corroborated by Decision 262 excerpts or operator materials. 

For Vinacomin/TKV’s small-to-medium coal fleet, the retrieved Vinacomin-linked industry source specifically identifies Na Duong 110 MW, Cao Ngan 115 MW, Son Dong 220 MW, Cam Pha 680 MW, Mao Khe 440 MW, and Nong Son 30 MW as CFB coal plants. Nong Son is excluded from the table because the requested threshold is >30 MWe, not ≥30 MWe. 

Nhon Trach 3 and Nhon Trach 4 are listed separately because they are distinct units/projects within one LNG-to-power development package. PV Power materials identify ongoing EPC/PPA/GSA implementation for Nhon Trach 3&4; the combined table capacity is 1,624 MWe. 

O Mon 1 is classified as Domestic gas despite historic fuel-oil operation because Decision 262/PDP8 implementation treats the O Mon complex in the domestic gas/Block B chain. This row is therefore an operating plant with a fuel-conversion/status note rather than a pure greenfield domestic-gas row. 

Quang Tri appears twice for different concepts: the 1,320 MW coal BOT project, whose extension/review status appears in a PDP8 implementation appendix excerpt, and the 340 MW Quang Tri combined-cycle gas turbine project using Báo Vàng domestic gas. These are not duplicate rows. 

Kiên Giang 1 and Kiên Giang 2 are retained as shelved domestic-gas historical candidates because the MOIT/VEPG PDP8 background report notes inadequate gas supply for Kien Giang I&II. They should not be treated as active firm PDP8 projects without a newer provincial/MOIT approval. 

Capacity reconciliation within the table: Pha Lai 1 plus Pha Lai 2 equals 1,040 MWe; Duyen Hai 1 equals 2 × 622.5 = 1,245 MWe; Duyen Hai 3 equals 2 × 622.5 = 1,245 MWe; Vinh Tan 2 equals 2 × 622 = 1,244 MWe; Nhon Trach 3 plus Nhon Trach 4 equals 1,624 MWe; Long Son 1 plus Long Son 2 equals 3,000 MWe; Son My 1 plus Son My 2 equals 4,500 MWe.
